claim: The AVC Patent Portfolio License is structured as a multi-licensor single-transaction alternative to bilateral SEP licensing; patents are submitted for independent expert essentiality evaluation; new licensors/patents may be added during the current term at no additional royalty.
metric_value: multi-licensor pool; independent essentiality evaluation; no extra royalty for added patents during term
notes: Structural facts about the pool mechanism. Reinforces that pool economics are portfolio/program-scoped, not single-patent priced.

claim: Via LA publishes AVC decoder/encoder OEM royalty steps of $0 for the first 100,000 units/year (one affiliated entity), $0.20/unit for units 100,001–5,000,000, and $0.10/unit above 5,000,000, with an enterprise cap of $9.75M/year in 2017 and after; FAQ states royalties do not increase or decrease because of an increase or decrease in the number of AVC Essential Patents.
metric_value: $0 / $0.20 / $0.10 unit steps; $9.75M enterprise cap (2017+); rate independent of patent count
notes: Pool/program economics only. Must not be treated as the price or attributable value of US6825782 or any single SEP.

claim: Via LA publishes an extensive public roster of AVC Patent Portfolio Licensees in good standing spanning consumer electronics, mobile, PC, broadcast, streaming and software vendors (examples include Apple Inc., Google LLC, Microsoft Corporation, Samsung Electronics Co., Ltd., Sony Group Corporation, Netflix, Inc., Amazon Digital Services, Inc.).
value_carrier: AVC/H.264 compliant products and services ecosystem
metric_value: large multi-industry public licensee roster under one portfolio license
notes: Shows real-world pool uptake / product-ecosystem scale at the program level. Via LA itself warns that listing a company does not prove which of its products are licensed; this ledger does not map US6825782 to any named product.
